advances:
Adds the first boundary-completion inequality for a single
\(A_0\)-polygon.  Two adjacent trace intervals force a lower bound on
the interior-side derivative of the third chord profile.  Concavity and
the area of the outer cap give an upper bound on the same derivative.
For the \(p_k=0\) boundary this yields
\[
2\Delta d\,
\bigl(\gamma L-(\delta-\beta-L)K\bigr)_+
\le
K^2(\delta-\beta-L)(\delta-\beta).
\]
The exact offsets proposed for the new strict-trace calibration violate
this inequality by a large rational margin.  Hence no convex \(A_0\)
with those trace intervals and areas exists, and the failure persists
through an open neighborhood of the proposed offsets and lengths.

proof:
We first prove a two-interval boundary-completion lemma.  Work in affine
coordinates \((R,T)\) with the same coordinate-area Jacobian
\(\Delta\).  Suppose a compact convex polygon \(C\) has full sections
\[
C\cap\{T=0\}
=\{(r,0):\gamma\le r\le\gamma+K\},
\tag{13}
\]
\[
C\cap\{R=0\}
=\{(0,t):\tau\le t\le\tau+L\},
\tag{14}
\]
where \(\gamma,K,\tau,L\ge0\).  Let the physical area of
\[
C\cap\{T\le0\}
\]
be \(D\).

Assume first that \(\tau>0\).  The convex hull of the two intervals in
(13)-(14) lies in \(C\).  For \(0\le T\le\tau\), its section at level
\(T\) contains the interval between
\[
r_-(T)=\gamma\left(1-\frac{T}{\tau}\right)
\]
and
\[
r_+(T)=(\gamma+K)
\left(1-\frac{T}{\tau+L}\right).
\]
Let \(W(T)\) be the full \(R\)-chord length of \(C\) at level \(T\).
Then
\[
W(0)=K
\]
and
\[
W(T)\ge r_+(T)-r_-(T).
\]
Taking the right derivative at zero gives
\[
W'_+(0)
\ge
\frac{\gamma}{\tau}
-\frac{\gamma+K}{\tau+L}
=
\frac{\gamma L-\tau K}{\tau(\tau+L)}.
\tag{15}
\]
The polygonal chord profile \(W\) is nonnegative, concave, and
piecewise affine.  Its right derivative at zero is a supergradient.  If
the right side of (15) is positive, put
\[
G=\frac{\gamma L-\tau K}{\tau(\tau+L)}>0.
\]
Then for every \(T\le0\) in the support,
\[
W(T)\le K+W'_+(0)T\le K+GT.
\tag{16}
\]
Nonnegativity confines the negative side of the support to
\[
-\frac K{W'_+(0)}\le T\le0,
\]
and hence
\[
\Delta D
\le
\int_{-K/W'_+(0)}^0
\bigl(K+W'_+(0)T\bigr)\,dT
=\frac{K^2}{2W'_+(0)}
\le\frac{K^2}{2G}.
\tag{17}
\]
Multiplying (17) by \(2G\tau(\tau+L)\) gives
\[
2\Delta D(\gamma L-\tau K)
\le K^2\tau(\tau+L).
\]
If the numerator in (15) is nonpositive, the same statement with a
positive part is automatic.  This proves
\[
2\Delta D(\gamma L-\tau K)_+
\le K^2\tau(\tau+L).
\tag{18}
\]

If \(\tau=0\), (14) contains the origin.  Since (13) is the full
\(T=0\) section, it must also contain that origin, so \(\gamma=0\).
Equation (18) is then literal.  The same proof works when \(K=0\) or
\(L=0\) by taking singleton intervals or limits.  This completes the
two-interval lemma, including vertex-on-line cases.

Apply it to \(A\) with
\[
R=-Y,\qquad
T=p_k=\delta-X-Y.
\tag{19}
\]
This coordinate change has determinant magnitude \(1\) relative to
\((X,Y)\).  The diagonal trace (4k) becomes
\[
T=0,\qquad R\in[\gamma,\gamma+K].
\]
The horizontal trace (4l) becomes
\[
R=0,\qquad
T\in[\delta-\beta-L,\delta-\beta]
=[\tau,\tau+L].
\]
Under the exact support (2), the only positive-area cell on
\(T=p_k\le0\) is \(P_{k\ell}\).  Thus \(D=d\), and (18) is exactly
(7).

For (9), apply the same lemma with
\[
R=Y,\qquad T=X.
\]
The full \(T=0\) trace is
\[
R\in[\alpha,\alpha+J],
\]
the full \(R=0\) trace is
\[
T\in[\beta,\beta+L],
\]
and the only positive-area cell on \(T=X\le0\) is \(P_j\).  Substituting
\[
\gamma=\alpha,\quad K=J,\quad\tau=\beta,\quad D=a
\]
in (18) proves (9).

It remains to test the proposed data.  Equations (10)-(12) give
\[
\tau
=100-\frac{959}{10}-\frac15
=\frac{39}{10},
\]
\[
\gamma L-\tau K
=20\cdot\frac15-\frac{39}{10}\cdot\frac1{10}
=\frac{361}{100}>0.
\tag{20}
\]
The two sides of (7) are therefore
\[
2\Delta d(\gamma L-\tau K)
=\frac{361}{50},
\]
\[
K^2\tau(\tau+L)
=\frac1{100}\cdot\frac{39}{10}\cdot\frac{41}{10}
=\frac{1599}{10000}.
\tag{21}
\]
Since
\[
\frac{361}{50}
=\frac{72200}{10000}
>
\frac{1599}{10000},
\]
inequality (7) fails by
\[
\frac{70601}{10000}.
\]
This is the first boundary-completion equation that the proposed trace
intervals fail.  It rules out the exact data and, by continuity, all
sufficiently small perturbations of them.  No assertion about \(A_2\)
or compatibility separators is used.
statement:
Let \(A\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a two-dimensional compact convex polygon
in affine coordinates
\[
p_j=X,\qquad p_\ell=Y,\qquad
p_k=\delta-X-Y,
\qquad \delta>0,
\tag{1}
\]
with coordinate-area Jacobian \(\Delta>0\).  Assume the exact positive
support
\[
P_j,\qquad P_0,\qquad P_\ell,\qquad P_{k\ell},
\tag{2}
\]
and no other positive-area cell.  Write
\[
|P_j|=a,\qquad |P_0|=b,\qquad
|P_\ell|=c,\qquad |P_{k\ell}|=d.
\tag{3}
\]

Parameterize the full \(p_j=0\), \(p_\ell=0\), and \(p_k=0\) trace
intervals by
\[
A\cap\{X=0\}
=\{(0,y):\alpha\le y\le\alpha+J\},
\tag{4j}
\]
\[
A\cap\{Y=0\}
=\{(x,0):\beta\le x\le\beta+L\},
\tag{4l}
\]
\[
A\cap\{X+Y=\delta\}
=\{(\delta+t,-t):\gamma\le t\le\gamma+K\},
\tag{4k}
\]
where
\[
0\le\alpha\le\alpha+J\le\delta,
\quad
0\le\beta\le\beta+L\le\delta,
\quad
\gamma\ge0,
\tag{5}
\]
and \(J,L,K\ge0\).  Under the positive support (2), all three lengths
are positive.

Put
\[
\tau=\delta-\beta-L\ge0.
\tag{6}
\]
Then every such polygon satisfies the diagonal boundary-completion
inequality
\[
2\Delta d\,(\gamma L-\tau K)_+
\le K^2\tau(\tau+L).
\tag{7}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
2\Delta d\,
\bigl(\gamma L-(\delta-\beta-L)K\bigr)_+
\le
K^2(\delta-\beta-L)(\delta-\beta).
\tag{8}
\]

There is a symmetric vertical boundary-completion inequality
\[
2\Delta a\,(\alpha L-\beta J)_+
\le J^2\beta(\beta+L).
\tag{9}
\]
Both inequalities involve interval offsets and adjacent trace lengths;
they are not consequences of the separate chord bounds that retain only
\((a,b,J)\) or \((d,b,K)\).

All boundary cases are literal.  If \(\tau=0\), the horizontal trace
contains \((R,T)=(0,0)\) in the coordinates used below, so the full
\(T=0\) chord forces \(\gamma=0\); then (7) is \(0\le0\).  Likewise,
if \(\beta=0\), the vertical trace forces \(\alpha=0\), and (9) is
trivial.  If a trace interval is a singleton, the positive-part formulas
remain valid by continuity.  Vertices on either cutting line have zero
area and are included in the closed intervals (4).

For the proposed exact \(A_0\) data
\[
(a,b,c,d)=\left(1,\frac{59}{2},3,1\right),
\qquad
\delta=100,\qquad\Delta=1,
\tag{10}
\]
\[
J=K=\frac1{10},\qquad L=\frac15,
\tag{11}
\]
\[
\alpha=80,\qquad
\beta=\frac{959}{10},\qquad
\gamma=20,
\tag{12}
\]
inequality (7) fails.  Therefore there is no convex polygon with these
four exact cell areas and these three exact trace intervals.  Since the
failure is strict and every term in (7) is continuous while
\(\tau>0\), the same conclusion holds throughout some open neighborhood
of the data (11)-(12).
